stem: A nurse is monitoring pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP/PCWP) through a pulmonary artery catheter. What does this measurement primarily estimate?

options.A: Left atrial pressure and left-sided ventricular filling pressure.

rationale: Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is obtained by occluding a pulmonary artery branch and creates an indirect estimate of left atrial pressure. It is commonly used to assess left ventricular filling pressure. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Interpret PAWP/PCWP as an indirect estimate of left atrial and left-sided filling pressure.
source_locator: Introduction; Clinical Significance — left atrial pressure and LV filling/LVEDP surrogate
source_claim_supported: PCWP/PAWP is an indirect estimate of left atrial pressure and is used to assess left ventricular filling pressure when correctly measured.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — invasive hemodynamic monitoring and interpretation
correction_summary: Tightened the key to emphasize that wedge pressure is an indirect estimate/surrogate rather than a direct left-heart measurement and removed unnecessary claims about fluid status. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: NCBI directly supports A and warns that accurate wedge interpretation matters. B-D measure different physiologic variables. Independent second pass passed.
